# Chelus product site implementation plan

**Goal:** Build the approved editorial product site with dedicated setup, guide and reference routes for GitHub Pages.
**Architecture:** Static HTML generated by standard-library Python, shared templates and self-hosted assets. Output is deployable as files, with no browser router or runtime dependencies.
**Spec:** The first visual concept and four-section site structure approved in conversation; `website/README.md` records the maintained design and operation.

## Constraints

- Preserve burgundy/cream branding, serif display headings, fine rules and generous spacing.
- Agent runtime is on-device; inference is remote via DeepSeek. Keep pre-1.0 status and verification limits accurate.
- Do not change the agent's runtime or add dependencies to it.
- Every route must work directly under `/chelus/`, with accessible mobile navigation and usable code examples.
- Generated phone photographs are explicitly illustrative; replace with real owner photographs before launch if available.
- Local implementation and review are authorized. The user approved pushing the review branch and opening a PR; merge and deployment remain separate.

## Tasks

- [x] Build the static generator and shared shell. Verify root/project prefixes, internal links and fragments, asset presence, metadata, and 404 navigation with `python -m unittest discover -s website/tests`.
- [x] Implement the selected homepage and useful setup, guide (Telegram, memory/skills, tools/approvals, scheduling), and reference content, grounded in the README and source. Generate reference defaults from `Settings` AST, avoiding runtime imports.
- [ ] Add the Pages Actions workflow, local preview command, maintenance docs and existing README corrections. Verify desktop/mobile in the cloud browser, navigation, copy buttons and console errors. Compare the rendered homepage with the selected visual in one combined image.
- [ ] Run the full repository test suite and static build; review the complete branch, fix material findings, and commit the verified result locally. Ask for permission before public push/deployment.

## Review focus

Project-prefix links, direct nested navigation, mobile overflow and keyboard access, copy controls without JavaScript, documentation drift, and accidental release/portability claims.
